title: Role affinity model & scope boundary design for RBAC v2
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Context: RBAC v1 implementation has grown pragmatic but brittle: role semantics mix resource ownership, tenant scope, and transient session grants. RBAC v2 must provide a clear, auditable model that supports: 1) multi-tenant isolation, 2) fine-grained resource hierarchies (project, model, endpoint, dataset), 3) ephemeral scope elevation for admin tasks, and 4) compatibility with SSO/SAML group mappings and audit logging requirements.

Goal: Propose a role-affinity model where roles are typed (System, Tenant, Resource) and bound to explicit scope objects. Define scope boundary enforcement, resolution algorithm, and a permissions matrix for common product surfaces (Console, API, Dedicated, Private control plane). Ensure the model is provably auditable and minimally surprising for downstream policies (canary rollouts, emergency takeovers).

Non-goals: RBAC enforcement engine implementation details, UI surface polishing, and third-party IdP integrations beyond mapping rules (those will be separate tickets).
acceptance_criteria: A clear type system for roles: 'system', 'tenant', 'resource' with documented semantics
A canonical list of scope objects and their hierarchy (organization > tenant > project > model > endpoint > dataset)
Resolution algorithm which determines effective permissions given multiple role bindings and session-level elevations
A permissions matrix for at least 24 common actions across Console/API/Dedicated/Private
Design includes audit log entries schema and examples for grant/revoke, delegation, and emergency elevation
Mapping guidance for SSO/SAML group->role sync and conflict resolution rules
Security review sign-off recorded and acceptance tests defined for enforcement edge-cases
notes: Primary trade-offs considered: centralized role catalog (simpler ops) vs. tenant-local role definitions (better isolation). Recommendation below favors a small global catalog with tenant-scoped bindings to reduce operational surprises.
We must support 'ephemeral elevation' tokens for emergency admin tasks; these must be fully audited and limited by time and scope.
Session precedence: session-scoped grants > resource-scoped role bindings > tenant defaults > system defaults. Documentation will call this out and show examples.

Performance note: evaluation must be cache-friendly — the resolution algorithm will include a cached effective-privileges entry per (principal, scope) invalidated on role-binding changes. Engineering ticket for cache invalidation is a follow-up.
permissions_matrix_summary: Design includes a 24x6 matrix (actions x surfaces). Example entries: 'deploy_model' => requires 'tenant:deploy' or 'resource:owner' on project/model; 'view_billing' => requires 'system:billing_view' or 'tenant:billing_view' on tenant; 'override_rate_limit' => requires system admin or explicit session elevation.
resolution_algorithm: 1) Collect direct role bindings for principal at requested scope and all ancestors. 2) Collect group-based bindings from SSO mapping. 3) Apply session ephemeral grants (if present). 4) Compute union of allowed actions and deny precedence for explicit denies. 5) Short-circuit evaluate common fast-paths using cached effective-privileges. Edge cases handled: conflicting allow/deny, cross-tenant access, and delegated service principals.
audit_log_spec: Each grant/revoke/elevation event must produce a structured audit entry: timestamp, actor_id, actor_type (user/service), target_scope (org/tenant/project/resource), action (grant/revoke/elevate), previous_bindings (list), new_bindings (list), reason (free text), correlation_id. Examples included in design doc. Logs must be exportable to SIEM and retained per compliance policy.
sso_mapping_guidance: Support two primary modes: push (IdP->Redwood group sync) and pull (Redwood queries SAML assertions on login). Mapping rules support wildcard patterns on group names and explicit overrides. Conflicts resolved by prefer-explicit-binding then most-specific-scope. Admins can set 'mapping priority' at tenant level.
decisions: Adopt a mixed catalog model: a small global role catalog (privileged roles and primitives) plus tenant-local 'composite' roles that reference primitives. Use 'deny' as explicit precedence when present. Use token-based ephemeral elevation with 15m default TTL, max 24h with extra approval. Audit schema standardized and required for all modifiying events.
next_steps: Sync with Identity team to finalize SSO mapping API (meeting scheduled 2025-02-14)
Create ENG follow-up for evaluation cache invalidation (ENG-41348)
Draft API contract for role-binding endpoints and audit export (open PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rbac/pull/126)
Design Console UX flows for role binding and ephemeral elevation (DES ticket forthcoming)
comments: 2025-02-12 - Aisha Khan: Initial write-up complete. Pinned the candidate scope hierarchy in the design doc. TL;DR: favor small global primitive set + tenant composites.

2025-02-14 - Marco Li: Reviewed with Identity team. Action: Identity to provide group sync API contract by 2025-02-21. Noted SAML assertions may contain nested group membership; design will support role derivation from nested groups.

2025-02-20 - Priya Patel (Product): Requested explicit examples for Dedicated and Private control plane differences. Added three scenarios to the matrix: on-prem admin takeover, tenant-admin limited deployment, cross-tenant support team diagnostics.

2025-02-25 - Ethan Caldwell (Security): Raised question re: 'deny' semantics across inheritance. Decision: explicit deny wins, but we will add a linting job to catch surprising deny overlays prior to rollout.

2025-02-28 - Marco Li: Posted implementation plan draft and a link to prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rbac/pull/126. Prototype includes role enum, binding APIs, and a cache structure for effective-privileges.
2025-03-02 - Aisha Khan: Design updated with audit log schema examples and sample SAML mapping rules. Marking for security review scheduling.
